# spec/contract/literals

`spec/contract/literals` — the vector table's Call and Expected cells:
`hexDecode("66")`, `"f"`, `[00 0f]`, `Key = 00ff`, `L = 42`, `22 x 0b`,
`concat([00], [ff])`. A cell is read in two steps. First its text is
parsed into raw literals, which do not yet know whether a quoted string is
bytes or text. Then the callee's signature settles each one: a quoted
string where bytes go becomes `{ascii}`, and where a string goes `{str}`;
`L = 42` is the int 42 where an int goes and the byte 0x42 anywhere else.
Reading `"f"` the same way in both places would make the contract say
something the table does not.

Numbers keep their text: an int is its decimal digits (written as a JSON
string once it passes 2^53 - 1), and an f64 carries its text and the
binary64 encoding that text reads as.

Generated from [src/spec/contract/literals.ts](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/src/spec/contract/literals.ts).

## Declarations

### RawKind

The form a cell writes a literal in, before a type settles it.

```ts
enum RawKind
```

<scalar-field name="Bool" type="4">

`true` or `false`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="Bytes" type="1">

`[00 0f]`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="Concat" type="10">

`concat(a, b)`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="Empty" type="2">

`(empty)`: no bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="F64" type="6">

`1.5`, `-2e-3`, `NaN`, `Infinity`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="Int" type="5">

A decimal integer.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="Labelled" type="7">

`Key = 00ff`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="LabelledInt" type="8">

`L = 42`: an int where an int goes, else hex pairs when the digits are some.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="Null" type="3">

`null`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="Repeat" type="9">

`22 x 0b`: a run of bytes written `count` times.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="Str" type="0">

`"text"`: bytes or a string, as the type says.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="Words" type="11">

`[0x11111111 0x22222222]` or `State = [11111111 22222222]`: words of 4, 8 or 16 hex digits.

</scalar-field>

#### RawLiteral.words

A bracket's words as printed, when they are a word array (all 4, 8 or 16
hex digits, `0x` on every word or on none); empty otherwise. Bytes like
`[879531e0 c5ecf37d]` carry their words too, for a word-array type.

```ts
words: string[]
```

### LITERALS_PRINTABLE

What a command source's Expected may be: the kinds `spec/gates/run` compares with its output.

```ts
const LITERALS_PRINTABLE: string
```

### literalsPrintable

Whether a command source may expect a literal of this kind: bytes, a
string, an integer, a bool or null, each with one canonical text that
`spec/gates/run` compares with what the command printed. An f64 has no one
text, and words are bytes printed in groups.

```ts
function literalsPrintable(k: LitKind): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="k" type="LitKind" required>

the literal's kind

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

whether a command's output is compared with it

</scalar-field>

### literalsSettle

Settles a raw literal where a value of type `ty` goes. A quoted string is
`{ascii}` where bytes go and `{str}` where a string goes; an int where an
f64 goes is that f64's text; `L = 42` is an int where an int goes and the
byte 0x42 anywhere else. Every other literal is as written, for the caller
to judge against `ty`.

```ts
function literalsSettle(
  raw: RawLiteral,
  ty: string | null,
): Result<Literal, string>
```

<scalar-field name="raw" type="RawLiteral" required>

the literal as the cell writes it

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ty" type="string | null" required>

the value type it goes where, or null for a place no signature
  types (an argument past the last parameter)

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;Literal, string&gt;">

the literal, or why it cannot be settled

</scalar-field>

### literalsSettleVector

A vector's Call arguments and Expected value, settled and typed by the
callee's signature: as many arguments as parameters, each of its
parameter's type, every int in range, and an expected value of the return
type. Every refusal is given, not only the first.

```ts
function literalsSettleVector(
  fn: FnSig,
  args: RawLiteral[],
  expect: RawLiteral,
): Result<SettledVector, CellError[]>
```

<scalar-field name="fn" type="FnSig" required>
